page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs spanning 16 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz. The server contains 64.0 GB of memory, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio typical of high-density compute configurations. It includes an L3 cache of 35 MB and supports instruction set extensions such as AVX-512 with VNNI and AES cryptography. The instance has no local storage attached and includes a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth under a KVM hypervisor.

Benchmark data shows moderate multi-threaded performance alongside lower single-core execution speeds. In single-core workloads, stress-ng recorded a score of 1312.39, and single-threaded gzip compression measured 22.88 GB/sec, placing single-core throughput in lower percentile ranges. However, multi-threaded operations scale efficiently, demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 27992.16 and a PassMark CPU score of 27240.11. Memory throughput reaches 109.69 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 47.96 GB/sec for large-block writes. Key application benchmarks reflect steady mid-range throughput, such as 26.78 million Redis SET operations per second and 20.38 GB/sec in static web serving tests.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.c6.8xlarge instance is its modest per-core clock speed and single-threaded performance in exchange for reliable multi-core compute density. Without bundled local storage, persistent or ephemeral block storage must be attached externally over the network. The hardware profile offers balanced cost efficiency for parallelized, CPU-heavy tasks that do not demand extreme memory capacity or dedicated GPU acceleration. This instance is suitable for compiling software, batch data processing, web serving clusters, microservices, and general compute workloads capable of leveraging multi-core parallelism.
